title: Canary Safety Broker: Learning-based Trigger Composer for Graceful Model Rollbacks
creator: Claire Zhang
description: Problem: Current canary rollouts rely on static thresholds for individual SLOs (p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, token cost, and throughput) which produces brittle behavior: noisy signals cause oscillatory rollbacks, risk-prone aborts for low-impact token-cost spikes, and poor handling of cohort-specific regressions. We need an orchestration layer that composes multiple signals into a single, explainable safety score, learns per-customer/cohort baselines, and exposes tunable hysteresis so rollbacks are effective yet minimally disruptive.
goal: Deliver a Canary Safety Broker that (1) computes a composite safety score from multiple SLO inputs, (2) adapts thresholds using online bayesian/EMA baselining per cohort, (3) supports graded remediation actions (throttle, divert, shadow, rollback), and (4) integrates with the Console for visibility and manual override.
success_metrics: Reduce false-positive auto-rollbacks by >= 60% in simulated noisy traffic
Decrease mean time to safe-remediation for real regressions to < 3 minutes
Maintain <5% increase in incident blast radius vs manual rollbacks
Instrumentation: availability of composite safety score and per-signal contributions in Console for 100% canaries
acceptance_criteria: Broker computes a single 0..1 safety score from latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput with explainable per-signal weights
Adaptive thresholding module learns baseline per-cohort (user-id, region, route) and updates thresholds without human intervention; admins can pin or override
Three remediation actions implemented and exercisable: reduce canary traffic to 10%, divert to previous model, and full rollback to pinned version
Safety hysteresis implemented to require sustained breach for N minutes or M requests before auto-action
Simulation harness and chaos tests demonstrating robustness across synthetic noise patterns (Poisson traffic bursts, token-cost drift, intermittent GC spikes)
Telemetry surfaced in Console: timeline of score, active remediation, justification log entries, and links to related traces/PRs
Manual abort/force-rollback controls available in Console with audit logging and RBAC enforcement
implementation_notes: We will build this as a lightweight control plane component that subscribes to the existing rollout telemetry stream. Core pieces: (1) signal normalizers for each SLO type, (2) composite scorer (configurable weighted sum + anomaly multiplier), (3) adaptive threshold learner using Bayesian posterior updates and short-term EMA, (4) hysteresis engine with min-duration and min-sample guards, (5) action executor that calls rollout API (scale, divert, rollback), (6) audit & explainability logs for each decision.
risk_mitigation: Start with 'observe-only' mode for 2 weeks across 10% of canaries; expose score but do not take actions. Use conservative priors and require multi-signal agreement before any automatic remediation. Add kill-switch to disable auto-actions per org/route. Schedule a security review for the control plane's API auth and audit streams.

Prototype composite scorer with configurable weights and per-signal contribution outputs
Build adaptive threshold learner: bayesian priors + EMA baseline module
Developer tests: unit + integration + simulation harness
UI: Console panel for safety score, logs, and manual controls
E2E: rollout flow where broker can exercise scale/divert/rollback actions
Run observe-only experiment for 2 weeks, collect KPIs and refine priors
Flip to canary-auto mode gradually with conservative rules and sampling
steps: Design data schema for normalized signals and score payloads
Implement scoring service in Go (sidecar or control plane microservice)
Add HTTP hooks and RBAC checks for action execution
Create simulation jobs to generate noise and cohort-specific regressions
Add Console UI and permit feature-flag rollout (ff: canary_safety_broker)
Run observe-only across 10% canaries; iterate priors and weights
Enable limited auto-remediation for low-risk routes, expand after validation
